messages:
Ivy (CSM): FYI Peregrine procurement sent back the security questionnaire. They want explicit answers and a snapshot of evidence by Friday COB. They flagged SOC2 boundary, encryption/KMS options, and subprocessors.
Ravi (Security): can you drop the specific questions here?
Ivy (CSM): short list: 1) Is the hosted inference API covered by your SOC2? 2) Can customers bring their own KMS on Hosted? 3) Do you accept tokenized PANs for inference? 4) Provide list of subprocessors and a snapshot date.
Jules (Infra): brief: Hosted uses Redwood-managed KMS; customer-managed keys are available for Dedicated and Private only. We should avoid saying "never" in docs.
Tara (Legal): I'll craft firm language that doesn't create obligations. Proposed: "Redwood's SOC 2 Type II report covers the hosted control plane and hosted inference service as documented in our compliance binder. Dedicated and Private deployments have contract-specific control boundaries and available evidence; customers should contact their account team for deployment-specific artifacts."
Ravi (Security): good. For KMS: "Hosted: Redwood-managed KMS. Dedicated/Private: customer-managed KMS/HSM supported under contract." Add sentence about encryption at rest and TLS in transit.
Ivy (CSM): can we make a 2-3 sentence vendor-form answer for each Q so procurement can paste? Short, copyable.
Ravi (Security): drafted snippets: 
Q: Is Redwood SOC2 certified?
A: Yes. Redwood maintains a SOC 2 Type II report covering our hosted control plane and hosted inference service. For Dedicated or Private deployments, control boundaries and evidence may differ; please request deployment-specific artifacts from your account team.

Q: Can customers provide their own KMS?
A: Redwood supports customer-managed keys and HSM integrations for Dedicated and Private deployments. The Hosted API uses Redwood-managed KMS; please contact your account team to discuss contract options for enhanced key control.

Q: Do you accept payment card data?
A: Customers must de-identify or tokenize cardholder data prior to sending it to Redwood endpoints. Redwood does not process or retain primary account numbers (PANs) in plaintext. If tokenization is not feasible, please engage Redwood Security to evaluate an isolated Dedicated or Private deployment under contract. (Subject to contract.)

Q: Subprocessors and residency
A: Attached is a snapshot of Redwoods subprocessors (snapshot date 2026-03-18). Our subprocessors page is maintained publicly and customers can request change notifications per their contract. Data residency options are offered for Dedicated and Private deployments; Hosted residency is provided by region selection and associated contract terms.
Ivy (CSM): nice. small edits: remove the weird char in "Redwoods" and add links to binder + subprocessors page.
Ravi (Security): done. Link placeholders: https://redwood.example.com/compliance/soc2 and https://redwood.example.com/subprocessors. We'll swap with gated links when sending.
Tara (Legal): add the standard "subject to contract" and "no reliance" sentence: "The information provided is for informational purposes and is subject to contractual terms between Redwood and the customer."
compliance-bot: Reminder: attach latest DPA (v3.2) if DPA/contract language referenced.
Ivy (CSM): I have DPA v3.2 and current subprocessors export. I'll attach both. Also offer: do we want to propose a 30-day SOW signing extension if procurement needs time?
Tara (Legal): we can offer a one-time 30-day extension by request. Please draft the extension email and send to me for approval.
Jules (Infra): I'll attach a redacted KMS integration diagram for Private deployments. Ping me before sending so I can scrub hostnames.
Ravi (Security): quick nit on the PAN answer: change "process" -> "process or store" and call out TLS for transport.
Ivy (CSM): updated draft will go into the vendor form. Can I get approval by 2pm PT? Procurement says they need this in the next 36 hours.
Tara (Legal): I'll review by 1pm PT.
Ravi (Security): I'll sign off by 11am PT and share a final suggested paragraph for the security section.
Ivy (CSM): thanks all. If procurement still stalls, AE (Noah) is looped for potential escalation; he asked for a short "procurement unblock" note we can offer (30-day extension + pilot).
Jules (Infra): for the pilot option, Ops can enable a limited retention config for 30 days. Tech ops needs to approve but we can propose it.
Ivy (CSM): perfect. I'll collate the snippets, attach DPA + subprocessors snapshot (2026-03-18) + KMS diagram, and post a copy of the completed vendor form here for final sign-off before I send. :sparkles:
